subject: Unscheduled: hotfix for quantization-induced inference instability
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@acmeanalytics.com>, ops@acmeanalytics.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unscheduled: hotfix for quantization-induced inference instability

Tom / Acme ops team —

Quick heads up from the runtime team: we detected an intermittent inference stability regression tied to a recent quantization optimization. Symptoms: elevated token-latency for a subset of sessions and rare malformed completions when models are running with 4-bit quantized kernels on certain Dedicated clusters (not all customers). We traced the root cause to a kernel selection path that mis-handles grouped attention padding when sequence lengths are short.

Impact observed so far:
- Affected routings: Dedicated GPU pools with quantized model variants (4-bit) on Linux kernels x.y.z
- Client-visible: occasional 500/502 spikes and, in <0.05% requests, truncated outputs
- Scope: small percentage of requests for customers using low-latency quantized variants (Acme observed ~0.2% error rate increase)

Immediate action: we are preparing a hotfix (kernel-level patch) to revert the problematic selection heuristic and add a safety check. This is an unscheduled, short-notice deploy. We plan a staggered rollout: 10% -> 50% -> 100% across affected Dedicated pools. Estimated timeline: start in ~30 minutes, full completion within 45–60 minutes. We do not anticipate a prolonged outage; there may be short retries/502s for impacted endpoints during cutover.

What we need from you:
- No action required to keep your endpoints running.
- If you have scheduled high-throughput jobs in the next 2 hours that cannot tolerate transient retries, please let us know ASAP and we can coordinate a narrow maintenance window or route traffic to a non-quantized variant temporarily.
- After we complete the rollout we will ask you to run a short smoke test (attached verification_script.sh) and paste results or the verification_output_20280621.txt if you prefer.

Attachments: kernel_patch_v1.patch (diff/patch), verification_script.sh (bash script)

Escalation contact: Soojin Lee (runtime PM) — +1-415-555-0123, #incidents (Slack)

I will post updates in this thread as we progress. Sorry for the short notice — we want to get this fixed before it affects more requests.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Runtime Incident Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Tom Briggs <t.briggs@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled: hotfix for quantization-induced inference instability

Thanks Soojin — appreciate the quick flag. A couple quick questions:

1) Do you expect any state loss for active streaming sessions? We run a number of long-lived chat sessions and want to avoid user-visible truncation.
2) You mentioned routing to a non-quantized variant. Do you have a recommended fallback model id we can switch to automatically if we see an uptick?

We have a large batch job scheduled at 10:00 PT that we can pause if needed; please advise whether we should hold.

—Tom
Tom Briggs
Head of ML Ops, Acme Analytics

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 09:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unscheduled: hotfix for quantization-induced inference instability

Adding details from infra validation run — staging tests completed and patch behaves as expected:

- Staging run (models: redwood-llama-7b-quant4): 10k requests, no malformed outputs observed after patch.
- Expected customer impact during rollout: brief surge of 502s during the node restart/driver swap; typical recovery within ~45–90s per node.
- Rollout plan: 10% -> 50% -> 100% with 10–12 minute observation windows. We will halt and rollback if error rate > 0.5% above baseline for >10 minutes.

Mitigation options for Acme:
- If you need zero-retry guarantees for the 10:00 job, route to the non-quantized variant `redwood-llama-7b-fp16` temporarily. It has slightly higher cost but is not impacted by this kernel path.
- Alternatively, pause the job for ~1 hour and resume after we confirm completion.

I'll kick off the rollout now and post a timestamped status update at each stage.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Production Engineer | Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 21 Jun 2028 12:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Update: hotfix deployed and verification complete — followup/postmortem scheduling

Hi Tom / Acme ops —

Summary: rollout completed to 100% at 12:21 PT. Validation: we ran the attached verification_script.sh across a sample of your endpoints and captured the output (verification_output_20280621.txt). Error spikes subsided after the 50% ramp; post-rollout error-rate is within baseline. No evidence of state loss for streaming sessions beyond brief retries — we observed session reconnects that resumed normally.

What we did:
- Deployed kernel patch (kernel_patch_v1.patch) to the quantized selection path; added safety check for grouped-attention padding shapes.
- Staged rollout with observation windows and automated rollback thresholds (not triggered).
- Performed smoke tests against your staging and 3 production routing buckets for an aggregate 25k requests.

Customer action: please run the attached verification script on your side and paste the output if you want us to cross-validate. If you coordinated to pause the 10:00 job, you can resume now. If you routed to `redwood-llama-7b-fp16`, we will automatically route back to your original variant unless you request otherwise.

Next steps / follow-up:
- I will send a concise postmortem (root cause, timeline, action items) by EOD tomorrow.
- We’ve scheduled a 30-minute postmortem call for Tue 2028-06-25 11:00 PT; invite link: https://meet.redwood.ai/pm-2028-06-25-quant-fix
- We will include a permanent fix in next week's runtime patch release and a regression test in our CI to catch grouped-attention padding cases.

Thanks for your patience and quick coordination. If you see any lingering issues please reply here or ping #incidents.

Attachments: verification_output_20280621.txt

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Runtime Incident Lead | Redwood Inference
